# Tests: false-positive screen (ruff findings)

Part of SA-0MSSSNOZN000LQKR (Phase A — vertical slice 1). Test-first: this suite must be written and green BEFORE the screen implementation (F1).

## Goal

Prove the model-judged false-positive screen correctly classifies ruff findings from the Phase 1 code-quality scan into `genuine` / `confident-false-positive` / `uncertain`, records justifications in the audit report, and never triggers remediation for anything other than `confident-false-positive`.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A batched Pi call over ruff findings parses into per-finding classifications; a finding missing from the batch response falls back to `uncertain` (caution-first), never `confident-false-positive`.
2. Unparseable/provider-error screen output (Pi model failure, timeout, concurrency-limit marker) degrades to `uncertain` for ALL findings — no remediation can be triggered from a failed screen (no config change, no commit, no work item).
3. The screen is skipped entirely (zero Pi calls) when the code-quality scan yields no ruff findings; non-ruff findings (eslint, etc.) are never sent to the screen.
4. Justifications are recorded per finding and appear in the audit report output for all three classifications.
5. Medium/low confident-false-positive findings are classified and reported but the screen never proposes config remediation for them (remediation is blocking-severity only — see F2/T2).

## Minimal Implementation

- Extend `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_phase1.py` (or a new `test_audit_runner_false_positive.py`) with mocked Pi calls asserting classification parse paths and fallbacks.
- Add report-content assertions (screen classifications + justifications present in the persisted report / `_build_issue_json` output).
- Add skip-when-no-ruff-findings coverage in the existing phase-1 scan tests.
- Keep tests green under the existing mocked-runner conventions in `skill/audit/tests/conftest.py`.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_phase1.py` — existing Phase 1 scan tests to extend.
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_core.py` — report-output assertions may live here.
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — the screen under test (import target).
- `skill/audit/tests/conftest.py` — shared mocked-runner fixtures.

## Dependencies

- None (test-first; written before F1).

data.description:
## Goal

Prevent the audit runner's Phase-1 code-quality scan from passing non-Python files (YAML, JSON, Markdown, etc.) to ruff as explicit file arguments, eliminating false-positive `invalid-syntax` findings that get auto-created as work items.

## Background / Root cause

On 2026-08-11, an implement self-review audit ran `run_code_quality(files=cq_scope_files)` with the git changed-file list, which included `proxy/config-cheap.yaml` (uncommitted changes at the time). `_run_ruff_check` invoked `ruff check <yaml-file>` — ruff parses YAML as Python and emitted 121 false-positive `invalid-syntax` findings, which `create_epics_for_findings` auto-created as work items under the Quality Improvement epic (LP-0MSJFTRUW0076Z5Y). Those stale items were later marked completed/in_review and drained one-by-one by the herdr downtime audit tier (~59 dispatches in one evening).

The `.ruff.toml` `exclude = ["*.yaml", "*.yml"]` fix (commit 7580063) is **insufficient**: ruff only honors `exclude` for directory scans; explicit file arguments bypass it (verified: `ruff check config-cheap.yaml` with the exclude in place still returns invalid-syntax findings, while `ruff check .` returns `[]`).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `run_ruff` / `_run_ruff_check` filter the `files` list to Python extensions (`.py`, `.pyi`, `.ipynb`) before invoking ruff; non-Python files are skipped and never passed as explicit paths.
2. A regression test asserts ruff is never invoked with a `.yaml`/`.yml` file path when the changed-file list includes one, and that no finding work items are created for non-Python files.
3. Directory-scan behavior (`files=None`) is unchanged.
4. Genuine ruff findings on `.py` files are unaffected (existing tests pass).
data.title: Audit runner: filter non-Python files before passing to ruff

## Blocker: wl sync refuses to pull refs/worklog/data

**Symptom**

`wl sync` fails with: `✗ Sync failed: Refusing to merge worklog data from refs/worklog/remotes/origin/worklog/data: 117 incoming commit(s) fail the author-identity gate.`

Categories (from `wl sync debug` + gate output):
- ~108 commits: **empty author email** (author 'Sorra the Orc', no email) — latest Aug 15 20:28; earliest Aug 13-14 range
- ~9 commits: author email `ross@example.com` does not match configured user.email `pi@local`

`--allow-foreign-author` does NOT help: it explicitly 'never bypasses the empty-author-email gate', and the majority of commits are empty-email.

**Impact**

- No pull/push sync for the SorraAgents worklog at all — changes accumulate locally only (work items/comments land in the local sqlite store but never reach the git ref or remote); the remote diverges.
- New local items (e.g. SA-0MSW9Q08A0045GRV) cannot be pushed.
- Affects all SorraAgents wl operations relying on sync.

**Likely root cause / remediation options (to be investigated)**

1. Remote ref history was authored by an environment with no git user.email configured (empty), or with `ross@example.com` (some other machine config), while the local store uses `pi@local` (config.yaml / git config mismatch).
2. If the remote ref is the canonical history, rewrite/filter the ref (git filter-branch / git filter-repo author fix) so all commits carry the configured identity, then re-sync.
3. Check whether the wl store config (user.email) used to be `ross@example.com` in another working copy and whether 2) is safe; do NOT force-push without operator approval.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `wl sync` in SorraAgents completes successfully (pulls remote worklog data).
2. The author-identity gate passes for all commits on refs/worklog/data (no empty emails, no foreign emails).
3. Local items (e.g. SA-0MSW9Q08A0045GRV) push to the remote ref.
4. A documented decision on how future commits avoid empty-author-email (git config user.email enforcement / wl gate).

## Goal

Ensure `wl sync` is unblocked and record the operator-authorized provenance. Verified observation (2026-10-16): the remote ref `refs/worklog/remotes/origin/worklog/data` has already advanced past the 4 `pi@local` commits via correct-identity commits (`ebd7bb2e` → `fc9460c1`, 19:28–20:27 +0100); a plain `wl sync` now completes, `last-synced-ref` = `fc9460c1`, and the previously stranded item SA-0MV9JVLBQ0090RNC resolves locally.

This child therefore confirms the recovery end-to-end and records provenance; if the merge was performed by a session without operator authorization recorded, record the operator's explicit (a) choice here.

## Operator authorization (provenance)

2026-10-16: operator explicitly chose option (a) — one-time `wl sync --allow-foreign-author` — recorded in SA-0MVB57M02008QPJS Decisions + Appendix. A deliberate one-shot safety-gate bypass; record the exact command and output in a comment.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1** `wl sync` completes without an author-identity refusal: previously-stranded items (e.g. SA-0MV9JVLBQ0090RNC) are present in the local store and `last-synced-ref` advances past the 4 offending commits.
- [ ] **AC2** The one-time `--allow-foreign-author` remediation is operator-authorized and recorded in a comment with the exact command and output (safety-gate provenance).
- [ ] **AC3** A subsequent plain `wl sync` (no flag) is a no-op success (idempotent; gate satisfied because last-synced-ref is past the offenders).

## Notes

- Do NOT add `pi@local` to the allow-list as part of this item — that is a separate child (`Add pi@local to syncAllowedAuthors`). This item is the authorized one-time merge + its verification only.
- The 4 offending commits remain in shared history (66b8e59b is an ancestor of the tip); they are inert only because `last-synced-ref` is past them. A fresh clone with no `last-synced-ref` scans the whole history, so the durable fix is the allow-list child.
- The recovery is a prerequisite for pushing this plan's other child records and the parent's close to origin.

## Key Files

- `.worklog/last-synced-ref`, `.worklog/worklog-data.jsonl` (read-only verification)

## Dependencies

- Blocked-by: SA-0MVB57M02008QPJS (parent).

## Deliverables

- Successful sync + provenance comment with command/output; verification of last-synced-ref advance.

data.description:
Discovered blocker during audit of SA-0MSSSNOZN000LQKR children.

## Problem
ruff check . reports a critical F841 in skill/agent-log-review/tests/test_agent_log_review.py:1055: unused variable joined in _WlStub.__call__. Introduced by commit 7a880c20 (SA-0MV6UGWC4000GU0G).

## Why it blocks
Audits of the false-positive screen children run the Phase 1 code-quality scan. With a clean working tree the scan falls back to whole-repo scope and surfaces this genuine critical finding, blocking Phase 1 for every child.

## Fix
Remove the unused joined assignment in _WlStub.__call__ (test stub; no behaviour change).
